conditions.what: author's evaluation starts for R16: uniform draw from the evaluation bank (5 start families), as evaluate.py lines 50-54; nominal physics; the policy gets the simulator's exact part pose

same starts and same policy noise stream as REF, nominal physics; the part position given to the policy (env.observe part_p, env.py line 183, its only part input with part_q: rl/obs.py lines 108-113) is offset by 1.0 mm in the horizontal plane, a fixed calibration error per episode whose direction is drawn from the episode's seed and written in plan.json before any rollout. R16 entry tolerance: radial clearance 0.25 mm (hole r 8.25 mm, scene.py line 150; rod r 7.9975 mm, line 198) plus the rod's 0.5 mm chamfer (line 199). The simulator, its outcome predicate and the robot-side report are unchanged.

same starts and same policy noise stream as REF; sliding friction x0.25 on the gripper pads (PhysicsConfig.finger_friction, scene.py line 52; pad-part contacts use it through priority 2, line 312) and on the part (part_friction, line 51; priority 1, line 369); passed to BatchedAssemblyEnv(pcfg=...), env.py lines 87-91

removed_before_any_run.V1_LOOSE: 'loose' starts only. Not a change of conditions: 'loose' is one of the five start families the policy was trained and evaluated on (resets.py line 28; README line 56: 98.1 % at 12.5K iterations), so it was a slice of REF. Kept as REF's per-family breakdown (env_success_by_start_family). Review A3, 26/10/2026.

bank.source: upstream scripts/build_banks.py (README line 105 recipe, this task only)

timing_estimate: README line 108: 3200 episodes take about 1 h on 16 CPU cores (all 20 tasks, evaluate.py protocol), about 1.1 s per episode. tasks.py lines 74-78: a rod control step costs 1.0 against an all-20 mean of about 6.6 (gears and nuts on fine physics). Budget taken without that discount: 3 x 320 = 960 episodes, about 18 min if 16 vCPU = 16 cores, about 36 min if a vCPU counts as half a core.
caveats: Simulation only: MuJoCo, Franka Panda model, NIST board assets. No real robot, no transfer claim.

The controller (AssembleNIST policy) receives the simulator's exact part pose every step (env.observe, env.py lines 177-185; rl/obs.py) as if a perfect tracker existed. The robot-side report does not use it.

Outcome by the env's own predicate (env.py lines 225-227): keypoints within 1 mm, no simultaneous safety failure, 15 s limit. Episodes keep stepping to the horizon after their outcome is frozen (as evaluate.py line 64). The robot-side report is computed afterwards from the recorded signals: retrospective: computed after the full rollout from recorded robot-side signals; it picks its own report instant and never stops or changes the controller.

No force/torque or contact sensor exists in the model (panda.xml has none). Force is estimated from the commanded joint torques (PD, averaged over the control step, env.py line 146). Distances are those of the tool centre point (kinematic model), never of the part. The finger-joint opening is a joint reading, not an object width; the pad gap is an estimate from the model geometry (PAD_OFFSET, resets.py lines 29, 45-47).
Robot-side thresholds were fixed before any rollout and not tuned on these results.
V1_OFFSET changes only what the policy is told about the part (a 1 mm horizontal error of its exact pose); the simulated world and the robot-side report are those of REF.

'safety fault detected' and 'joint speeds within limits' are not scored: the env's safety flag (vel_violation | nonfinite, env.py lines 217, 220, 225) reads the same joint-velocity monitor as the robot (env.py line 145), so a score would be true by construction. They are reported as consistency checks. Audited: the main claim when it is 'inserted' / 'not inserted' (part pose) and 'part held' (finger-part contacts). Everything else in a report is a diagnostic, not independently audited (AUDIT_SCOPE).

audited_predicates.main_claim: 'inserted' / 'not inserted' against the part keypoints in the simulator at the report instant (the env's 1 mm threshold); 'still to check' is counted, never scored; 'safety fault detected' is a consistency check, not scored
audited_predicates.part_held: against geometric contacts of both fingers with the part (distance <= 0.5 mm) at the report instant; this does not prove a stable grasp or a sufficient holding force

diagnostics_not_independently_audited: joint speeds within limits (the robot's own joint-velocity monitor)
summed finger-joint opening and the estimated pad gap: joint readings, not a measured object width
tool position: tool centre point from the kinematic model, not the part
estimated axial push and descent: from commanded joint torques, not a force sensor

policy_actions: sampled (evaluate.py default), torch.manual_seed(0) before each condition
one_job_rule: one Job; any re-run is reported together with the first, never instead of it
